summary.text: 影 means “shadow.” Its conventional analysis is phonosemantic: 景 provides a sound cue and 彡 contributes semantic or graphic material. Historical accounts describe 彡 as added to the earlier shadow-writing 景 to distinguish the graphs, though the first design and early sequence are not securely documented.

formation.text: 影 is conventionally analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 景 supplies a sound cue, while 彡 contributes semantic or graphic material. Historical accounts describe 景 as an earlier writing for “shadow” and 影 as 景 with 彡 added, after which the written forms specialized. This supports graphic differentiation; it does not establish that 景’s shadow use began as sound-based borrowing or developed from its separate light sense.

components.text: 景 is the phonetic element in the conventional analysis. Modern Mandarin jǐng resembles 影 yǐng. The Middle Chinese forms share a rhyme but differ in initial notation; the Old Chinese forms differ in initial notation but share rising-tone notation. These comparisons support, but do not prove, the phonetic analysis. Historical accounts also describe 景’s use for “shadow” as a graphic counterpart to 影, without establishing a progression from its separate light sense.

sound_limitation.text: The current and reconstructed comparisons are compatible with the traditional phonetic analysis, but do not independently prove 景’s role in the original design.

sound.text: The modern Mandarin readings are similar, though their initials differ.
The Middle Chinese forms share a rhyme but differ in initial notation.
The Old Chinese forms differ in initial notation but share rising-tone notation.

components.text: 彡 is the visible graphic-semantic element in the conventional account and is associated with hair ornament or decorative markings. The evidence does not establish that it literally depicts lines of shadow.

history.text: Historical accounts describe 影 as 景 with 彡 added after 景 had been used for “shadow.” This supports graphic differentiation, but does not establish that the shadow use began as a phonetic borrowing of the whole graph 景.

The selected seal-style images are modern redrawings of 彡 and 景 shown separately. They illustrate the forms named in historical accounts but do not document a dated early form of the complete character 影.

uncertainties.text: The earliest appearance of 影 is disputed. Scholarship favors the 405 Eastern Jin 爨寶子碑, while a Han-end commentary and a lost Zhang Heng stele have also been proposed. The claim that Ge Hong first added 彡 comes through later lexicographic reports.

No secure sequence of early forms for the complete character is established. The sound comparison supports the conventional analysis but does not prove the original design; 景’s older shadow use is documented separately from its ordinary light sense and is better supported as a lexical and graphic counterpart than as a whole-character borrowing.

senses.text: A museum catalog transcribes 影命不長 on a rubbing of the 爨寶子碑 dated 405; the date and reading are mediated by the catalog and later scholarship.
Dictionary records include image-related uses such as figures or portraits. Their first dates and a complete development from “shadow” are not established.
影 is used with the sense “photograph”; the beginning of this use and its path from “shadow” are not dated here.

limitations.text: The first dates of image, reflection, portrait, and photograph uses, and the transitions among these senses and “shadow,” remain unresolved; no semantic-development link is assigned.
The 405 attestation is supported by a cataloged rubbing and later scholarship rather than direct inspection of a contemporary original. Earlier-attestation claims remain disputed.

overview.text: 影 means “shadow.” Historical accounts describe it as 景 with 彡 added to distinguish the shadow writing; the earliest form sequence is not secure.

components.text: 景 is the proposed sound element; its reading resembles 影’s, supporting but not proving this analysis.
彡 is associated with hair ornament or decorative markings; it is not established as a picture of shadow lines.

relationships.text: 景 is the phonetic element in the conventional analysis. Modern Mandarin has 景 jǐng and 影 yǐng; Baxter–Sagart gives comparable Middle Chinese and Old Chinese forms that differ in initial notation. These comparisons support but do not independently prove the historical role.
彡 is semantic or graphic material in the conventional account of 影. It is associated with hair ornament or decorative markings; the evidence does not establish that it depicts lines of shadow.
